summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied traditionally under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti (born 1941) is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Calcutta, the University of Delhi, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University and the University of Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Patna University, and he served as a teacher at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University from approximately 1999 to 2002 and at Virginia Commonwealth University from circa 2002 to 2017.

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He served as professor of Indian philology there from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and held posts at the University of Calcutta as Lecturer in 1937 and Carmichael Professor in 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw from circa 1965 to 1967.
Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and headed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from circa 1996 to 2002.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was affiliated with the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta in 1994.

Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) is a historian and philosopher. He studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University under Donald Anthony Low. He taught at the University of Melbourne and has served as a professor at the University of Chicago.

Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is an Indologist and historian. He earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he taught from 1991 to 2003 as Chair of Indian History after lecturing at the Kern Institute.
Divyaraj Amiya is an Indologist and linguist attested in 2026 as faculty at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Diwakar Acharya (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated under Ramananda Giri and at the University of Hamburg, he taught at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, and Kyoto University before joining the University of Oxford in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1882 to 1886 and later served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at St. Petersburg University from 1886 to 1890. He subsequently held a post at the Imperial University of Dorpat from circa 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Kunzang Pelden, and Jigdrel Changchub Dorje, 6th Dzogchen Rinpoche.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2000 and lectured at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2005.
